name: Opt out of the Customer Experience Improvement Program
summary: Stop Windows from sending hardware and usage patterns to Microsoft for product trends.
what: Sets the policy Turn off Windows Customer Experience Improvement Program, which opts every account on this PC out of the program.
benefit: Less usage data leaves the PC. Microsoft's own policy text says the program collects hardware configuration and how the software and services are used.
risk: Safe. Nothing stops working. Microsoft's policy text says the Inventory Collector and Application Telemetry are also off while this one is.
advice: Suggested for everyone. It is a documented opt-out and takes nothing away.
facts: Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Microsoft says the program does not collect names or addresses
Also switches off the Inventory Collector and Application Telemetry, per Microsoft's text for those policies
Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education
Revert removes the policy value

name: Turn off the Inventory Collector
summary: Stop Windows from listing your programs, files, devices and drivers and sending the list to Microsoft.
what: Sets the policy Turn off Inventory Collector. Microsoft says it also stops collection of install data through the Program Compatibility Assistant.
benefit: Your list of installed programs and drivers is no longer gathered for Microsoft's compatibility checks.
risk: Low. Microsoft uses the data to find compatibility problems, so a rare problem with an old program may take longer to be noticed on their side. Nothing changes in how programs run.
advice: Suggested if you want less data leaving the PC. It changes nothing you will see.
facts: Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Has no effect to switch on if the Customer Experience Improvement Program is already off, because that turns it off too
Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education
Revert removes the policy value

name: Turn off Application Telemetry
summary: Stop Windows from tracking how programs use its system components.
what: Sets the policy Turn off Application Telemetry. Microsoft describes it as anonymous usage tracking of specific Windows system components by applications.
risk: Safe. It takes effect for programs started after the change, and a restart covers the ones already running.
advice: Your choice. It is documented and harmless, and the Customer Experience Improvement Program setting already covers it.
facts: Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Microsoft says it is off anyway while the Customer Experience Improvement Program is off
Applies to programs started after the change
Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education
Revert removes the policy value

name: Turn off LLMNR name lookups
summary: Stop asking other PCs on the network what a name means when DNS has no answer.
what: Sets the policy Turn off multicast name resolution, which disables link local multicast name resolution (LLMNR) on every network adapter.
benefit: Your PC no longer sends and answers these multicast name queries on a local network, which is useful on shared or public networks.
risk: Low. Names are still resolved by DNS. On a small network with no DNS server that relies on LLMNR to find other PCs by name, those names may stop resolving, and an address still works.
advice: Your choice. Fine on a home network with a normal router. Skip it if you find other PCs by name on a network without DNS.
facts: Microsoft describes LLMNR as a secondary name resolution protocol that needs no DNS server
Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every adapter
Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education
Revert removes the policy value

name: Turn off the Filter Keys shortcut
summary: Stop the pop-up when the right Shift key is held for eight seconds.
what: Clears the flag that lets the right Shift hold switch Filter Keys on. Microsoft documents it as FKF_HOTKEYACTIVE, 0x4, in the FILTERKEYS structure.
benefit: A held Shift in a game or a long edit no longer slows or blocks your keys with a Filter Keys prompt.
risk: None. Filter Keys can still be turned on from Settings, Accessibility, Keyboard.
advice: Suggested for gamers and fast typists. Skip it only if you use the shortcut yourself to switch Filter Keys on.
facts: Changes only the shortcut flag, so the other Filter Keys choices stay as they are
Does not turn Filter Keys itself on or off
Applies to your account only
Revert puts back the value that was there before
